name: Vespid Dynamics Biological Sensor Network
description: A surveillance system using genetically engineered organisms — plants, insects, and microorganisms — as living sensor platforms. BSN organisms are designed to detect specific stimuli (chemical compounds, electromagnetic emissions, vibrations, biological agents) and respond with bioluminescent or chemical signals readable by Vespid's monitoring equipment. A district instrumented with BSN organisms has living walls that detect explosives, trees that sense electromagnetic emissions, and soil microbes that identify buried objects — all invisible to conventional counter-surveillance because they are, to every test, ordinary living things.
social_impact: BSN has made the natural world a potential intelligence asset in ways that fundamentally challenge the concept of secure outdoor communication. When the grass might be listening and the trees might be watching, the paranoia is not unfounded — it is technically justified. The technology has driven a renewed interest in fully sealed environments for sensitive conversations and a growing market for biological counter-surveillance.
story_hooks: A BSN-instrumented park has been providing intelligence on everyone who passes through for two years — the organisms are so integrated into the ecosystem that even knowing they exist does not help identify which plant is the sensor.
BSN organisms have been discovered outside their designated monitoring zone — they are spreading naturally, extending Vespid's surveillance coverage without authorization or control.
